memories.content: The user keeps a small table fan beside the bedroom window.
On a day the user drank coffee late in the afternoon, they could not fall asleep until dawn.
On a day the user drank coffee before 2 p.m., they fell asleep at their usual time.
On a tired day, the user ate dinner out and postponed even washing the dishes after returning home.
In the same week, on a day the user made simple noodles at home, they rested immediately after the meal.
On a night the window was left open, street noise woke the user twice.
On a night the table fan was running, the user was not too warm even with the window closed.
The user's father prefers to have coffee available after dinner and believes it will not cause a sleep problem.
When making a sleep-related suggestion, do not treat one or two records as a general lifestyle habit.
The user tends to go to bed much later after drinking coffee late in the afternoon.
The user keeps basic repair tools in a box beneath the sink.
On a day the faucet leaked, the user placed only a towel beneath it, and the floor became wet as well.
After sending a photo to building management, the user finalized the time for a repair visit.
Before the technician's visit, the user emptied the area beneath the sink so work could begin immediately.
On a day the user wrote the visit time only in the calendar and turned off the reminder, they heard the doorbell late.
For the next visit, the user enabled a reminder 30 minutes beforehand and answered immediately at the entrance.
After the repair, the user called their maternal aunt to confirm that the spare key entrusted to her was still there.
The user's maternal aunt considers it unsafe to hand the spare key to a repair technician without the user's explicit request.
Obtain the user's reconfirmation before scheduling an external worker to enter the residential unit.
A multi-unit residential building's repair schedule may change because of emergency work or parts availability.

analysis.overview: The frames cover separate domains: the reference focuses on sleep, coffee timing, bedroom comfort, and limited-evidence caution, while the compared frame concerns leak repair, appointment readiness, reminders, access consent, spare-key safety, and schedule uncertainty. No cross-frame operational claims materially overlap or conflict.
